# Research references used for the model split

1. J. B. Allen and D. A. Berkley, “Image method for efficiently simulating small-room acoustics,” JASA 65(4), 1979. The suite uses a deliberately low-order, image-source-inspired early-reflection pattern rather than a measurement-grade solver.
2. R. Stoughton, “Measurements of small-caliber ballistic shock waves in air,” JASA 102(2), 1997. This motivates an independent N-wave projectile event.
3. S. D. Beck et al., “Variations in recorded acoustic gunshot waveforms generated by small firearms,” JASA 129(4), 2011. This supports separating muzzle blast, ballistic wave and environmental reflections, and motivates correlated per-shot variation.
4. E. M. Salomons, “Analytical model for sound of explosives and firearms,” JASA 156(3), 2024. This supports muzzle directivity and a positive/negative impulsive waveform model.
5. Audiokinetic Wwise documentation on voice priority and virtual voices. This supports keeping room tails, casings and distant details lower in priority than direct attacks and near projectile events.
6. Modal-synthesis literature for impact sounds: an impulse/noise excitation driving decaying modes is a compact physically motivated model for material identity.

The implementations are perceptual game-audio approximations, not forensic or hearing-safety simulators.
